The half-ellipse above is defined by the parametric equations 

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

What is the domain of the parameter $\theta ?$
worked_solution:
The parametric equations of an ellipse centered at the origin with a horizontal radius of length $a$ and a vertical radius of length $b$ are

$$
x=a\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=b\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

In our case, $a=5$ and $b=3.$ Therefore, the parametric equations of the *full* ellipse are

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [0,2\pi ).
$$

To restrict the parameterization to a half-ellipse, we associate the parameter $\theta $ with the central angle formed by a point $(x,y)$ on the ellipse and the $x$-axis. 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14040724/assets/5a028284d29850a9561a589c0e9fbf85e2e10e4e7a23d4ab46a765f492955b4f.png)

We can see that if we restrict $\theta $ to $[\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}]$, we get the half-ellipse.

Therefore, the parametric equations of the half-ellipse are 

$$
x=5\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,\,y=3\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta ,\,\theta \in [\frac{\pi }{2},\frac{3\pi }{2}].
$$
